frontMatter.title: Phase 10 evidence: fleet metadata, usage provenance, bounded content, VIBES evidence and installation inventory (fleet-evidence row)

summary: Phase 10 built the governed fleet metadata path on feature/mega-maestro-v1.1.0-rc in the Maestro checkout (macOS, Darwin 27, Node v26.12.0, git 2.54.0): the lifecycle projector (metadata-only run-state and decision events from the real desktop capture and the headless turn recorder), the durable event journal (one sequence across restarts, digest ids that dedup a replay, cursors with honest completeness, every gap counted), the authenticated telemetry client (one event per endpoint telemetry request, received only from a durable receipt, a lost answer resent under the same id, a policy denial a hold and never a drop), usage provenance (estimated or unavailable, never a zero the stream did not carry, priced under a named rate table revision, attributed to the org of record), bounded content capture under the endpoint collection profile and a signed per-role ceiling (exact original and derivative digests, a redacted derivative only, VIBES evidence under full_vibes alone, shed and revoke by count), the VIBES recorded graph from real run-states, and the installation inventory (detection apart from enforcement, subagents observed or unavailable, every gap named). Phase 10 added 51 tests in 07/08 over those seams. Deterministic coverage over the real projector, the real journal files, the real telemetry client, the real content capture, the real inventory module and the real socket client is green (24 targets, 45 files, 736 tests; the library suite 69 passed and the certifiable pair skipped for CP-01, CP-02 and the approval producer). The journey was exercised for REAL on this host over real producers and the real transport (projector, journal file, telemetry client, host adapter port, socket client, registration and attachment over a unix socket) against a LABELED DOUBLE of the daemon whose telemetry operation validated every report with the sibling's real @mega-maestro/contracts package and the runtime gate transcribed from apps/endpoint/src/spool/runtime.ts: five of six events received once each by id, sequence, time, family and boot, the inventory withheld by family, a resend answered duplicate, a dropped connection recovered after re-attach, a foreign boot refused unauthenticated, the VIBES and prompt digests recomputed independently, no canary on the wire. The real sibling daemon in its container (the same harness as phases 04 to 09, library 0.21.0 this time) again answered every step denied or unavailable: unenrolled, no approval producer, zero events ingested, so NO central event, usage figure or hash exists to compare against the observed sources. The endpoint of this build takes no inventory family from a runtime, carries no content and installs no ceiling (CP-01), the usage producer is not yet wired to the desktop process stream (Maestro-owned, named), and TRACE and vault have no producer on either side of this phase. The fleet-evidence acceptance row is therefore NOT passed; the fixture journey is recorded as positive evidence at the Maestro boundary, not as the pair.

realFixtureRun.what: The fleet metadata journey over the REAL Maestro producers and transport on this host, against a LABELED DOUBLE of the endpoint daemon. Real: createLifecycleProjector (PAIR_INSTALLATION), createEventJournal over a temp file, createTelemetryClient, the host adapter telemetry port (createManagedHostAdapter), createLocalEndpointClient registered (challenge, redeem) and attached over a unix socket with telemetry negotiated and required, telemetryReportOf, createUsageCapture, createInstallationInventory (readContractsPin on the real vendor path: absent), createContentCollectionSource, createContentCapture, buildVibesRecordedGraph, vibesEvidenceOf, a verified context from the pair verifier. Double: fakeEndpoint.ts (the daemon protocol transcribed from the sibling: envelopes, per-socket sessions, correlation replay, registration handshake) whose telemetry operation validated every report with the sibling's real contract package (@mega-maestro/contracts dist, read-only, zod incomingMetadataEvent) and applied the runtime gate transcribed from apps/endpoint/src/spool/runtime.ts lines 523-527 (binding), 530-534 (families, profile, references, provenance, identities) and 544 (revision), then answered the contract's durableReceipt (validated with the sibling schema too). Labeled too: the admission reference on the start (hand-built; the dispatch bridge is phase 04 to 06 evidence), the account reference (a digest handed in; the real resolver reads the agent layers), the content ceiling (installed by the harness: no endpoint operation installs one, CP-01).

two passes at batchSize 4: sent taken 4 received 4; sent taken 1 received 1 withheld.family 1; then idle. The double's spool holds exactly the five runtime-family events in projector order (agent.lifecycle#1, agent.lifecycle#2, agent.lifecycle#3, agent.lifecycle#4, usage#5), each report equal to its event by sequence, occurredAt, bootId epoch-pair, instanceId inst-pair, deviceId enr-pair, policyRevision 3, family (usage for the usage event, agent.lifecycle otherwise) and usageProvenance (estimated for usage, unavailable otherwise), every report parsed by the sibling incomingMetadataEvent (contractValidated true); zero denials at the double. Journal delivery {"pending":1,"uncertain":0,"received":5}, held 0; the received entries in the file are exactly the spool ids; the inventory entry stays pending with attempts 0. Canaries: the prompt, the sk-ant token, the /Users path, the account digest, org-pair, the model, agent/run/thread ids, the surface words, the token count and the cost appear nowhere on the wire; the journal file keeps the detail (token, path), the account digest and the org by design, and the prompt nowhere (it was never a fact field).

centralComparison.required: Compare central events, usage and hashes to the observed sources (the manifest fleet-evidence row).
performed: Observed sources: the real projector's six events and the real journal file (ids, sequences, times, delivery states) on this host.

Against the endpoint DOUBLE's spool over the real socket: five of six ids present once each with equal sequence, occurredAt, bootId, instanceId, deviceId, revision, family and provenance; the inventory id absent (withheld by family, pending in the journal with zero attempts); a resend answered duplicate; every report and receipt parsed by the sibling's real contract package.

Against the sibling contract schemas directly: the inventory fact parses as fleetInventory and an incomingFleetEvent envelope built from it is valid, while the runtime gate refuses the family; the content references parse as contentReference.

Hashes: the VIBES evidence sha256 recomputed independently from the canonical lines equals the content fact's original digest and the held bytes' digest; every event id is a digest of its fact (a replayed fact is the same id, shown in events.test.ts and usage.test.ts).
notPerformed: Against the REAL endpoint, ingest, worker, server or API: the daemon is unenrolled and ingested zero events, so there is no central record of any event, usage figure or hash (realPairRun).
Usage against a provider's billing record or the gateway meter: a runtime report says estimated or unavailable only, by contract; no gateway ran.
VIBES attestation, TRACE evidence binding and vault custody: no producer on either side in this phase (openDependencies).

The fixture journey took three attempts: the first failed to load (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, the shared imports were written two directories up); the second ran 4 of 5 cases and failed the recovery case because the composition's re-attach negotiates execution alone, so the telemetry standing after the dropped connection was no-standing (the fix: re-attach with telemetry negotiated and required, which is what the first attach already did). The runner rewrote steps-fixture.json and vitest-fixture.log on each rerun, so those two attempts are recorded here from their output and not as separate logs.

MRC-10-07 first focused run (Working/10-07-vitest-focused.log): two test-side mistakes, a backoff assertion that expected one report where the double records every attempted report (four of the same id), and a reporting assertion that expected single-event where the capture names a known provider's reporting up front (per-step for pi); both corrected in the tests before commit f4d48a6af / 93456febf. Second run green (Working/10-07-vitest-focused2.log).

MRC-10-08 first focused run (Working/10-08-vitest-focused.log): two count mistakes in the VIBES tests (10 window events, 6 records); corrected before commit c61265b16. Second run green (Working/10-08-vitest-focused2.log).
The phase 04 to 09 pair runs remain under their own Working/*-verify folders.

deterministicCoverage.doubles: The endpoint daemon (fakeEndpoint.ts over a real unix socket, and the in-memory hostDouble of the adapter's two telemetry members in telemetry.test.ts), scripted timers, the identity view (ManagedIdentityView literals), the enrollment status (literals and pairStanding over the real port), the account reference resolver, the installed-provider reader, the content ceiling documents (installed by the tests), the capability snapshots. Everything else is real: the projector and its three fact validators, the journal over real temp files (load, attach, take, acknowledge, settle, page, trim, gaps, flush, restart over one file), telemetryReportOf and readTelemetryReceipt, the telemetry client (pump, hold, backoff, wake, drain, timers), describeUsageProvenance and the rate tables, buildUsageFact and createUsageCapture, the content source standing and parseContentCollectionCeiling, createContentCapture (digests, redactSecrets derivative, hold, shed, revoke, forget), buildVibesRecordedGraph and the VIBES annotation id rule, createInstallationInventory and readContractsPin, the enterprise service composition, the IPC handler and preload for enterprise:inventory, the headless runtime-host composition, the desktop capture listener and the content capture listener.
